title: fix: allow Mouse Without Borders pairing across valid Microsoft signer certificates

proposed_comments.body:
### Identify the actual signer-fixture search locations

**Severity:** `low` (non-blocking test diagnostics)

The helper probes curated Windows system executables as well as dependencies in the test-output directory, but its failure message says only "beside" the known signed dependency. Include both search locations and identify that dependency as the certificate comparison baseline, so a failed run points to the fixture sources that were actually examined.

Keep the hard failure and all existing identity, certificate and signature checks unchanged; this is only a diagnostic improvement, not a request to skip this regression.

```suggestion
            Assert.Fail($"No trusted Microsoft-signed peer with a leaf certificate distinct from {knownSignedPath} was found among the Windows system candidates in {Environment.SystemDirectory} or dependencies in {AppContext.BaseDirectory}.");
```

confidence.rationale: Exact helper searches Windows system candidates and test-output DLLs, whereas its failure message mentions only beside the baseline dependency.

proposed_comments.title: Identify the actual signer-fixture search locations
Let Release end-to-end tests exercise mixed product signers
proposed_comments.body:
**Severity: Medium — the Release end-to-end harness rejects the configuration this PR is intended to support.**

**Affected code:** `Assert-MwbEndpointSignatures` in `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/MouseWithoutBorders.UITests/Scripts/MwbTestSigning.ps1`, called by `Scripts/Initialize-AutonomousHost.ps1` and `Payload/EndpointWorker.ps1` before product startup.

**Problem:** Production `MeetsSigningPolicy` now permits independently trusted Microsoft leaf certificates, but the Release harness still unconditionally requires identical MWB/Settings certificate hashes. A consistent signed product build with distinct legitimate leaves therefore fails provisioning before the pairing test can run.

**Why it matters:** The new unit regression can pass while the two-endpoint suite cannot exercise the real mixed-signer product scenario. This is a test-harness compatibility gap, not evidence that the production repair itself has run end to end.

**Suggested change:** Align the normal signed-product gate with the independently verified product-signer policy:
1. In `Assert-MwbEndpointSignatures`, remove only the final unconditional MWB/Settings raw-certificate equality clause and retain the Runner/Settings file-version comparison.
2. Keep the loop's valid-signature/expected-publisher checks and its per-component `$TestCertificate.RawDataSha256` pin unchanged. That existing pin must still require every component to use the explicitly supplied test certificate.
3. Update the final error message to describe a version mismatch, and add separate normal-product mixed-leaf and explicitly pinned test-certificate cases. Do not remove all hash checks or relax test-certificate pinning globally.

**Verification:** Cover a normal Release set with distinct valid product leaves, invalid/tampered signatures, mismatched Runner/Settings versions, and a supplied test certificate with one wrongly signed component. Then run the two-endpoint pairing regression on a signed mixed-leaf product build. The current gate's same-leaf control, mixed-leaf rejection and invalid-signature rejection were exercised with controlled signature objects; this is branch evidence, not real-signature or VM execution.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The failing Release gate and its tests are outside the current PR diff; changing the production signature-policy hunk would not repair test provisioning.

confidence.rationale: Both Release startup callers execute the exact unconditional leaf-equality gate; controlled execution confirms rejection even when all preceding signature/publisher checks pass. Real signed-product VM validation remains required.
